evidence.curator_note: PRODUCTIVE PATH, step 1 (the main rightward arrow of eq 8.8). Ionized methyloxirane (n-ionized at oxygen, O+. localized per convention B) opens its ring: the O radical drives cleavage of the epoxide C-C bond (map 2 - map 4) to form the ring-opened distonic oxocarbenium CH3-CH=O(+)-CH2. (a primary carbon radical, map 4). This is a radical-site (alpha-type) cleavage: the bond broken (C2-C4) is incident to C2, the same atom on which the new C2=O3 pi bond forms. ARC COUNT: the book draws 3 arcs on the ring structure -- move <1> = O odd electron (map 3) into the forming C2=O3 pi bond; move <2> = one C2-C4 sigma electron into that pi bond; move <3> = the other C2-C4 electron onto the terminal carbon (map 4). All three fishhooks are drawn. Same nominal mass (m/z 58) as the precursor -- an isomerization, not detected as a separate peak.

PRODUCTIVE PATH, step 2 (the reversible 'rH' equilibrium arrow, drawn as two half-arrows). The primary carbon radical of the distonic ion (map 4) abstracts a gamma-H (map 5) from the methyl group (map 1); coupled to this the C1=C2 pi bond forms and the C2=O3 pi bond opens, relocating the radical onto oxygen to give the more stable methyl vinyl ether (methoxyethylene) radical cation CH2=CH-O(+.)-CH3. ARC COUNT: the book draws 3 arcs in the middle structure -- a large arc carrying the H (map 5) from carbon 1 over to the radical carbon (map 4), a fishhook forming C1=C2, and an arc opening C2=O3 onto oxygen. For complete electron balance this is encoded as 5 fishhooks: moves <1,2> build the new C4-H5 bond (C4 odd electron + one C1-H5 electron), move <3> routes the other C1-H5 electron into the new C1=C2 pi bond, move <4> routes one C2=O3 pi electron into C1=C2, and move <5> puts the other C2=O3 pi electron onto oxygen as the new radical. Moves <3> (the second half of the H-transfer) and <4> are the parts condensed into the drawn arcs; no arc is fabricated. Reversible (drawn with a two-way arrow).

PRODUCTIVE PATH, step 3 (the downward 'rH' arrow from the enol-ether ion). A second hydrogen rearrangement: the vinyl H (map 6) shifts from C2 to C1 while the C1=C2 pi bond and an oxygen lone pair build the C2#O3 triple bond and the O3-CH3 (map 4) bond homolyzes, expelling a methyl radical (map 4) and giving the very stable acetyl (acylium) cation CH3-C#O(+), m/z 43 (35% of the 70-eV spectrum; loss of methyl). ARC COUNT: the book draws 3 arcs on the enol-ether structure -- one in the H/C=C region (left), one in the C-O region (centre), and one from oxygen out to CH3 (right, the O-CH3 homolysis expelling .CH3). For complete electron balance this is encoded as 7 arrows: moves <1,2> shift the C1=C2 pi into the C2-O3 bond (first new pi of the triple bond), move <3> is the oxygen lone pair (a full 2-electron arrow) forming the second new pi, moves <4,5> homolyze O3-C4 (one electron onto the departing methyl radical, one back onto oxygen to pair its radical into a lone pair), and moves <6,7> carry H6 from C2 to C1. The three printed arcs are the drawn subset; the remaining arrows (lone-pair pi donation and the completion of the H-transfer/homolysis) are the implicit balance, not fabricated arcs.

Cross-linked to MØD rules IMS_8_8_1, IMS_8_8_2, IMS_8_8_2b, IMS_8_8_3; ALL VERIFIED against their DFS (my map: C1=orig methyl, C2=orig ring CH, O3=oxygen, C4=orig ring CH2; the DFS use their own numbering). step_ring_opening = IMS_8_8_1 '[C]1(H)(H)(H)[C]5(H)[O+.]7[C]8(H)(H){-}5 >> [C]1(H)(H)(H)[C]5(H){=}[O+]7[C.]8(H)(H)': removes the {-}5 epoxide C5-C8 ring bond, forms C5=O7, C8 becomes the radical -- exactly the ring opening (their C5=my C2, C8=my C4, O7=my O3). MATCH. step_rH_to_enol_ether = IMS_8_8_2 '[C]1(H2)(H3)(H4)[C]5(H6){=}[O+]7[C.]8(H9)(H10) >> [C]1(H2)(H3){=}[C]5(H6)[O+.]7[C]8(H9)(H10)(H4)': H4 migrates from methyl C1 to C8, C1=C5 forms, O7 becomes the radical -- exactly this step (their H4=my map 5). MATCH; IMS_8_8_2b is the same interconversion written in the reverse direction (this step is flagged reversible). step_rH_methyl_loss = IMS_8_8_3 '[C]1(H2)(H3){=}[C]4(H5)[O+.]6[C]7(H8)(H9)(H10) >> [C]1(H2)(H3)(H5)[C]4{#}[O+]6.[C.]7(H8)(H9)(H10)': H5 migrates from C4 to C1, C4#O6 triple bond forms, the O6-C7 bond breaks releasing .CH3 (C7) -- exactly this step (their C4=my C2, O6=my O3, C7=my C4, H5=my map 6). MATCH. No geometry mismatches were found for the eq 8.8 rules.
